categories.main_business_segments: Sempra operates through three main reportable segments: Sempra California (including San Diego Gas & Electric Company and Southern California Gas Company), Sempra Texas Utilities (primarily equity interests in Oncor and Sharyland Utilities), and Sempra Infrastructure (energy infrastructure assets in the U.S. and Mexico, focusing on LNG, energy networks, and low carbon solutions). SDG&E and SoCalGas each have one reportable segment focused on regulated electric and gas utility operations.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company’s core technologies include electric transmission and distribution systems, natural gas distribution, transmission and storage infrastructure, LNG liquefaction and regasification facilities, renewable energy generation (wind and solar), and advanced grid and pipeline management systems. Sempra Infrastructure utilizes large-scale EPC contracts for LNG and pipeline projects, and is investing in low-carbon solutions such as hydrogen, carbon capture, and grid modernization.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Sempra’s primary customers are residential, commercial, industrial, and wholesale utility customers in California and Texas, as well as major energy companies, government entities, and industrial users in the U.S., Mexico, and global LNG markets. SDG&E and SoCalGas serve over 21 million people in Southern California, while Oncor delivers electricity to over four million Texas customers. Sempra Infrastructure serves utilities, energy marketers, and industrial customers globally, especially in LNG and pipeline services.
categories.geographic_coverage: Sempra’s operations are concentrated in Southern California (San Diego and Los Angeles regions), Texas (notably Dallas-Fort Worth and surrounding areas), and Mexico (Baja California, Sonora, Nuevo León, Chihuahua, and other states). The company also has significant LNG and pipeline assets in Louisiana and Texas, with global LNG export reach to Europe, Asia, and Latin America.
categories.supply_chain_position: Sempra operates primarily in the midstream and downstream segments of the energy supply chain, focusing on transmission, distribution, storage, and delivery of electricity and natural gas, as well as LNG liquefaction and export. The company also has upstream exposure through renewable energy generation and some gas procurement, but its core business is regulated utility and infrastructure services.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Sempra’s strategic focus is on expanding and modernizing energy infrastructure to support reliability, safety, and the energy transition toward cleaner sources. Key R&D and innovation themes include grid modernization, wildfire mitigation, renewable integration, LNG export growth, low-carbon fuels (hydrogen, biomethane), carbon capture, and digitalization/cybersecurity. The company aims to achieve net-zero scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions by 2050 and is investing in advanced energy technologies and partnerships.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through regulated utility rates for electric and gas transmission and distribution, long-term contracts for LNG liquefaction and regasification, pipeline transportation and storage fees, and power purchase agreements for renewable energy. Additional revenue streams include asset optimization, commodity sales, and storage services, with a significant portion of revenues subject to regulatory approval and cost recovery mechanisms.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Sempra’s main competitors include other large regulated utilities (e.g., PG&E, Southern California Edison, CenterPoint Energy), independent transmission developers, and global LNG and pipeline operators (including state-owned and multinational energy companies). Sempra is positioned as a leading North American energy infrastructure company with strong regulated utility franchises and a growing international LNG and energy networks platform, competing on reliability, scale, and clean energy transition capabilities.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of June 2024, Sempra’s market capitalization was $48.1 billion, with 2024 earnings attributable to common shares of $2.8 billion and total revenues exceeding $13 billion. The company has a robust capital expenditure plan, with $12.5 billion expected in 2025 and $41.4 billion over the next five years, reflecting growth in regulated rate base and infrastructure investments. Recent years have shown steady earnings growth, driven by utility rate base expansion and infrastructure project development.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Sempra emphasizes safe, reliable, and increasingly clean energy delivery, leveraging its scale, regulatory expertise, and infrastructure investment capabilities. Its value proposition centers on stable cash flows from regulated utilities, leadership in the North American LNG export market, and a commitment to innovation and decarbonization. The company differentiates itself through its integrated platform spanning utilities and infrastructure, focus on energy transition, and ability to deliver affordable, reliable, and lower-carbon energy solutions.
